underscore-normalization.note: Systemic normalization gap (cross-cutting, not DED-specific). Starling encodes diacritics in ASCII with a trailing underscore (e.g. in_r_u = Burrow iṉṟu, ir_r_ai = iṟṟai, cir_ai = ciṟai). _normalize_for_match stripped diacritics via NFKD but left underscores, so Starling and Burrow forms never reconciled, producing 'language matched but headword mismatch' rows. Fixed by adding '.replace("_", "")' to _normalize_for_match in both starling_tree_validator.py:89 and burrow_entry_parser.py:198 (kept in sync). 0/34,875 Burrow headwords contain underscores, so the change is strictly additive on the Starling side -- no regressions possible. Impact: entries_matched 13,793->14,383 (+590 rows across ~299 DEDs); entry_match_rate 70.3%->73.3%. Residual ~140 underscore rows still mismatch on other divergences (special vowels e.g. Toda twās_/twɨd_y, leading retroflex r_ placement, secondary parenthetical forms) -- out of scope for this fix.

length-dot-normalization.note: Systemic normalization gap (cross-cutting, not DED-specific). Burrow marks vowel length with a raised dot after the vowel (te·l = tēl, twa· = twā, aŋga·l = aŋgāl); Starling encodes the same length as a macron over the vowel, which _normalize_for_match already removed via NFKD + strip-combining. The dots are standalone (non-combining) characters, so they survived normalization and Starling/Burrow forms never reconciled -- producing 'language matched but headword mismatch' rows. Two visually-identical confusables occur: U+0387 GREEK ANO TELEIA (1,071 in matched forms, dominant) and U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT (3; what DED 2891 uses). Fixed by adding a _LENGTH_DOTS translate table (U+00B7, U+0387, plus IPA length marks U+02D0/U+02D1) applied after .lower() in _normalize_for_match, in both starling_tree_validator.py and burrow_entry_parser.py (kept in sync). Matcher-side only -- stored corpus headwords keep their dots, so no corpus regen needed, and the change is symmetric (Starling is already length-agnostic via macron-stripping), so no regressions. Impact: entries_matched 14,383->15,004 (+621 rows; 555 exact, 61 loose-substring of the projected cohort); entry_match_rate 73.3%->76.4%. Diagnosed from DED 2891 (Kota tēl/te·l, Toda twās_/twa·s̱).

eng-velar-nasal-normalization.note: Systemic matcher-side normalization gap: Starling writes the velar nasal as eng (U+014B). Burrow uses n+combining-dot-above (U+1E45), which NFKD reduces to plain 'n'. Eng has no decomposition so it survived normalization, causing false-positive headword mismatches (e.g. 2591/Tulu, 3014/Kannada taggu vs taggu, 63/Tamil). Both are notational variants of the same phoneme - not a data divergence. Fixed by folding eng to 'n' via _ENG_FOLD translate table in _normalize_for_match in BOTH starling_tree_validator.py and burrow_entry_parser.py (matcher-side, no corpus regen). entry_match_rate 76.4 to 77.6, entries_matched 15004 to 15226 (+222). Residual eng rows that did not clear have additional genuine divergences (special vowels) and are left as genuine divergences.

ded-letter-suffix-normalization.note: Burrow's DDSA page numbers DEDR split-entry 4896 as '4896(a)' (and mislabels its (b) sub-entry as '4896(a)' too, yielding two corpus copies). Fixed matcher-side: _clean_ded_number now strips a trailing parenthetical letter (^(\d+)\s*\([a-z]\)$ -> base) so '4896(a)'/'4896(b)' index under '4896'. naiki-dialect-qualified-abbrev.note: The parser silently dropped every Naiki attestation. Burrow marks Naiki as 'Nk. (Ch.)' (vs. Naikri 'Nk.'), but _LANG_CHAR forbids the internal space, so all four _PATTERNS stopped the abbrev at 'Nk.' and failed on the ' (Ch.)' before the headword -- ~314 markers across the corpus, in all three wrapper forms ( 259, bare 54, 1). (Ch.)' = Naiki) else strip it to the base abbrev. The strip also correctly recovers ~25 bibliographic-tag markers ('Te. (SAN)', 'Ka. (DCV)', 'Ta. (lex.)') as their base languages, previously dropped too. Corpus regen: +327 attestations (Nk. (Ch.) +298, Te. +14, Ka. +6, Tu./Ma./Ta. +3 each), 0 losses. entries_matched 15,235->15,449 (+214), entry_match_rate 77.6%->78.7%, not_attested branches 690->668. Parser-side, corpus regenerated. nested-tag-headword-bold.note: Pattern A (Lang. headword) required the headword run to end at , so any nested tag inside the headword's bold span broke ([^<]+) and silently dropped the language -- no fallback recovered it (Pattern E's (?) blocks it; B/D needs a separate ). Three markup flavors, one root cause: nested obl. grammatical qualifiers (DED 1 Tu./Te./Pa./Konda), italicised scientific names (DED 62 Ma./Tu. Sphaeranthus indicus), and ... encoding artifacts (DED 11 To.). 613 dropped languages / 703 attestations across the corpus. Fixed parser-side: Pattern A terminator -> (?=<) (stop the headword run at the next tag, nested or closing -- transparent for clean markup), plus trim a trailing '(' artifact in headword cleaning (431/703 recoveries needed it). v8 reparse: +703 attestations (To. 132, Pa. 72, Kui 56, Te. 52, Kol. 45, Ko. 43, Ta. 41, Ma. 40, Pe. 39, Konda 38, Ka. 33, Nk. 26...), 0 losses, 0 headword-value changes for already-parsed languages (verified by faithful in-memory sim). entries_matched 15,449->15,841 (+392), entry_match_rate 78.7%->80.7%, fully_attested 5,404->5,617, not_attested 668->518. Parser-side, corpus regenerated. Deferred siblings (separate root causes): Kuwi-type text-before- (48), To-type abbrev mid-italic/malformed source (17).

kuwi-type-embedded-forms.note: Pattern A/C/B-D/E all require Lang's headword to follow within the same bold span or a cleanly-separated headword right after ; none tolerate a stray sitting between and the headword's tag. To. em) remains open -- same drilled DED 5154 surfaced both, but To-type needs a separate fix since the language marker isn't at the start of its span.

Validator: entry_match_rate 84.3%->84.6%, entries_matched 16,540->16,615 (+75). One known residual: DED 1147 (a)). Ka. headword-qualifier-after-lang-marker.note: Pattern A's headword capture (\s+([^<]+)(?=<)) didn't skip an optional dialect-qualifier parenthetical glued between the closing language marker and the headword when both share the same span (e.g. Go. (Tr.) aḍrai id. in DED 107, Kuwi (S.) aḍḍe ānai in DED 83). The captured headword text then included the leading (Qual.) string, and the downstream headword-cleanup filter -- which drops any captured string starting with ( as a bogus qualifier-only token -- discarded the whole attestation, silently dropping an otherwise-valid language match. Fix: added a shared _OPT_HEADWORD_QUALIFIER constant (the same qualifier-skip already used by Patterns B/C/F) to Pattern A, with a mandatory \s+ boundary kept before it rather than \s* -- Pattern A's capture has no literal anchor tag downstream to stop it from swallowing adjacent prose, so an initial \s* version introduced false-positive languages from italicised non-language tokens glued directly to following punctuation with no space (Artocarpus, Cyprinus, Grammar, Nāyadh.); caught via the corpus-regen diff and corrected before shipping. Net effect: +63 attestations / 59 entries gained, 0 losses; entry_match_rate 84.6% -> 84.9%, entries_matched 16615 -> 16657.

nested-tag-headword-bold-bcf.note: Patterns C, B/D, and F's headword capture (([^<]+)) required the headword to end at a literal with zero tags inside, so a nested grammatical qualifier (pl., obl.) mid-headword broke the match and silently dropped the language entirely (e.g. DED 5440's Kuwi: Kuwi (F.) vegū (pl. veska)). Same root-cause family as the already-fixed Ma-type bug (af90534), which only patched Pattern A -- Patterns B/D, C, F had the identical weakness, confirmed still present today (DED 1's Go. had the same shape and was still missing). Fix: a new _HEADWORD_SPAN_ACROSS_NESTED capture spans across nested non- tags instead of stopping at the first one, then strips the nested-tag markup during headword cleanup (_HTML_TAG_RE). Unlike Pattern A's simpler (?=<) lookahead (safe because its headword has no closing tag of its own), this needed an additional guard: a naive span-across-everything-except- version caused a regression, swallowing a DIFFERENT language's own NextLang. marker into the PRECEDING language's still-open headword span whenever that span did not close until after the next marker (DED 4900: muŋgi pōtu. Go. -- Go. vanished, swallowed into a bogus Ga. headword). Caught via a full-corpus old-vs-new parser diff before regenerating the real corpus. Fixed by adding a second negative lookahead that blocks spanning into Uppercase... (a language marker) while still allowing lowercase grammatical qualifiers through. Net effect: +163 attestations / 121 entries, 0 losses. entry_match_rate 84.9% -> 86.6%, entries_matched 16657 -> 17003 (+346).

primary-dialect-marker-gloss-truncation.note: Burrow's consolidated multi-dialect entries (Go., Kuwi, Kui) cite their first dialect's form immediately after the language marker with its own parenthetical, e.g. Kuwi (F.) vegu (pl. veska), (Su. Isr.) vegu..., (P.) vergu..., (S.) weggu.... The (F.) marker for that primary citation sits exactly where the existing headword-qualifier-skip mechanism (shared by Patterns A/B/D/C/F) treats it as a generic qualifier and discards it during parsing -- so it never survives into the stored gloss. The matcher's dialect-recovery mechanism (_extract_gloss_forms_for_abbrevs, the same one behind the previously-shipped Kuwi/Kui inline-dialect-citation fix) only finds markers that DO survive in the gloss ((Su. Isr.), (P.), (S.)), so when matching a specific Starling dialect like Kuwi (Fitzgerald) whose own marker was the consumed primary one, it falls back to a direct headword match using the full untrimmed gloss as meaning -- bleeding every later dialect's citation text into what's displayed for an otherwise-correct match, and tripping a false meaning_mismatch flag in the triage queue. Sized corpus-wide: ~1108 Go. + 1035 Kuwi + 41 Kui entries structurally exposed. Fixed matcher-side only (no parser change, no corpus regen): a new _truncate_gloss_before_first_marker trims the displayed meaning at the first dialect marker when matching a tracked dialect's primary form, deliberately returning empty when there's no text before the first marker (more honest than showing unrelated text, and avoids the false-positive flag since _is_meaning_mismatch treats an empty side as nothing to compare). Caught and fixed a related bug along the way: both call sites in _validate_branch/_validate_branch_direct had if matched_burrow_gloss: vr.burrow_gloss = matched_burrow_gloss, which silently discarded an intentionally-empty truncation result and fell back to the same untrimmed att.gloss -- fixed by using matched_burrow_gloss unconditionally whenever get_inline_abbrevs_for_starling_dialect applies. No entry_match_rate change (86.6%, as expected for a display-only fix) -- row_issues/triage queue dropped from 5567 to 5161 (-406 rows). Two new, separate findings surfaced and deliberately left open: Manda/Kui (not tracked as dialects of anything) have their own _recover_attestation_gloss_from_full_text boundary-extension bug; several already-tracked dialects (Maria Gondi, Parja Kuwi, Pengo, Sunkarametta Kuwi, Kuwi (Israel)) get a clean but semantically-empty extracted form because Burrow elides their gloss via a shared id. reference to the primary form, a pre-existing gap in the already-shipped inline-dialect-extraction mechanism.

periodless-language-gloss-boundary.note: _recover_attestation_gloss_from_full_text (duplicated in repair_burrow_corpus_glosses.py and starling_tree_validator.py) recognizes the next language has started via a regex requiring a trailing period ([A-Z][A-Za-z]+.) -- but Konda, Kui, and Kuwi are the only three language names in the whole inventory written without a trailing period, so the scanner silently walks past them and keeps extending the gloss into their text. Confirmed via DED 5440: Mand.'s parser-level gloss is correctly short ('pl. ) id.'), but the corpus-repair step's recovered gloss bled all the way through Kui and Kuwi's own citations into '...weska dry wood.' Fixed by adding Konda|Kui|Kuwi as recognized boundary alternatives in both copies. Caught a regression while verifying: a literal cross-reference mention -- DED 3246's '...(cf. Kui treba; with loss of t-)...' inside Kuwi's OWN gloss -- isn't a real attestation boundary, but the naive token match treated it as one, truncating Kuwi (Israel)'s recovered gloss before reaching its own '(Isr.) revu path (animal)' citation and flipping that match from Yes to Language only (entries_matched 17003 -> 17002). Confirmed via full corpus scan this is the only such cf. + period-less-name occurrence. Fixed by skipping a period-less-name match when immediately preceded by cf. -- re-verified via full corpus diff: only that one row changes back (Language only -> Yes), no other regressions, entries_matched restored to 17003. No entry_match_rate change overall (gloss-only fix, 86.6% throughout) -- row_issues/triage queue: 5161 -> 5154 (-7 rows, net of fixing the regression). One new, narrower finding surfaced and deliberately left open: the existing id.-chain resolution in parse_language_sections only substitutes a real meaning back in when an attestation's gloss is exactly 'id.' or starts with 'id.' -- it doesn't handle a leading grammatical note like '(pl.) id.' (DED 5440's Mand./Kui), so those rows still show the literal id. placeholder instead of the chained-back real meaning.

qualified-id-chain-resolution.note: Qualified-'id.' gloss chain resolution. Burrow glosses of the form '(qualifier) id.' -- a grammatical/sense qualifier (e.g. '(pl.)', '(obl. am-)') glued onto an 'idem' reference -- were matched by neither existing id.-resolution case (g == 'id.' / g.startswith('id.')), so the attestation displayed the literal qualifier + 'id.' placeholder instead of the chained-back real meaning. Fixed with a _QUALIFIED_ID_RE pattern plus a _LEADING_PAREN_RE strip (so chained links like DED 5440 Konda->Pe.->Mand. each show '(own qualifier) base meaning' without accumulating prior links' qualifiers), added to both burrow_entry_parser.py and repair_burrow_corpus_glosses.py (parser + repair, kept in sync). ~200 attestations match the shape; 0 '(...) id.' residue corpus-wide after the fix. Examples: DED 5440 Mand. -> '(pl.) firewood, fuel.', DED 5154 Pa. -> '(obl. am-) we.', DED 3729 Tu. -> '(obl. nuta-) 100.'. Gloss-display-only: entry_match_rate unchanged 86.6%, entries_matched 17003, triage queue unchanged. The prior session paused this fix uncommitted over a suspected 3-case regression (literal 'id.' at DED 5154/3729). Re-verified this session via a 3-stage pipeline trace (parser -> repair pass1 -> pass2) + corpus-wide scan: the regression does NOT reproduce (0 residue); the prior isolation experiment ran on an inconsistent code state. A defensive pass-1 guard (stop _recover_attestation_gloss_from_full_text clobbering a resolved gloss with raw 'id.' text) was prototyped and REJECTED -- it caused real gloss data loss (truncating long glosses past the parser's 200-char cap, e.g. DED 2237 Go. 277->212, DED 3398 Te. 304->208) and introduced 3 new '(...) id.' residue at DED 178; reverted in favor of shipping the original fix unchanged.

totype-embedded-marker.note: To.-type embedded language markers. Malformed DSAL markup where a language abbreviation sits at the END of an span (after lowercase qualifier or scientific-name text) with no /( immediately before the -- the closing lands after the abbrev instead of before it, so no anchored pattern (A/B/D/C/F/E) could reach it and the whole language was dropped. Two real shapes: sense-qualifier-before-abbrev (DED 5154 '...am<-> incl.). To.') and scientific-name-before-abbrev (DED 5 'Tu. agase-mara Agati grandiflora. Te. (B) agase-...'). Fixed parser-side with a new _STRICT_PATTERNS list (one bold-headword To.-type pattern) gated by a new _is_known_lang_abbrev allow-list check in _find_all_lang_spans -- because the pattern scans into an span it lacks the Abbrev anchor, so without the known-language gate italic citation titles/botanical authorities (Volume, Sanskrit, Linn.) were captured as bogus languages. id-expansion-overglue.note: RESOLVED 2026-08-17 (option A'). Both id. resolvers (burrow_entry_parser.parse_language_sections and repair_burrow_corpus_glosses.repair_corpus) previously copied the ENTIRE previous attestation gloss; on a multi-FORM antecedent this over-glues (DED 7 Ka. opened with all of Toda's gloss). Scores: A' leave = 0 corruptions; B head = 74% correct but 26% fabricated-wrong (50/192); C nearest = 40% correct, 60% wrong (antecedents often end in their own id./citation); D whole-copy (old) = 100% wrong on multiform. Under honesty>completeness, shipped A'. Fix: textnorm.antecedent_is_multiform(); both resolvers guard resolvable = last_real_gloss and not multiform -> single-form resolves as before, multiform keeps literal 'id.' (faithful to Burrow). Guard can only SKIP resolution, never assert a new meaning. Verification: corpus regen changed 202 glosses (all toward literal id./cleaner); validator diff vs baseline = 0 rows added/removed, entry_match_rate 94.0% held, entries_matched 18184->18185 (+1), 3 Match-status changes ALL positive (DED 4847 Seoni Gondi Language-only->Yes; DED 5554 Kui & DED 7 Kannada an-gal upgraded gloss_secondary->substring/exact), 0 matches lost; 141 rows changed only in displayed Matched Burrow meaning.
